name: Ningombam Borish Singh
tagline: Computer Science undergraduate building AI-driven systems — from computer vision on construction sites to explainable models for medical imaging.
summary: Computer Science undergraduate specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, with hands-on experience across AI research, computer vision, technical documentation, and full-stack development. Proficient in React.js, Next.js, Node.js, Express.js and PostgreSQL, and skilled at translating machine learning workflows into scalable, user-facing systems — as well as documenting the research behind them clearly. Currently researching explainable deep learning and hybrid CNN architectures for medical image analysis.

research.title: An Explainable Hybrid CNN Model with Adaptive Feature Fusion for Skin Lesion Diagnosis
research.description: Exploring an explainable deep learning approach for skin lesion diagnosis using hybrid CNN architectures and adaptive feature fusion, focused on discriminative feature extraction, model interpretability, and diagnostic performance.

projects.name: SafeSight — Intelligent Workplace Safety Monitoring
projects.description: An AI-powered construction site PPE monitoring system: custom-trained YOLOv8m for PPE detection and worker-level compliance tracking, with rule-based equipment association, video tracking, a RAG-based natural-language assistant over inspection data and PPE manuals, and automated PDF reporting with an interactive compliance dashboard.

projects.name: Campus Navigation System — IIT Ropar
projects.description: Production-grade interactive campus navigation platform integrating Leaflet.js mapping, REST APIs, and PostgreSQL-backed navigation data, with a directed A* routing engine, Yen's k-shortest-paths, an admin panel, and PWA/SEO/accessibility hardening.

projects.name: Skin Disease Prediction System
projects.description: Deep learning-based skin disease classification system trained on 11,000+ images across seven disease classes, enabling image-based diagnosis with class-wise prediction probabilities for interpretable confidence scores.

personality.description: Curious, ambitious, technical, occasionally overthinking, and permanently ready to start another project.
strengths: Can turn random ideas into projects
weaknesses: Sometimes debugs bugs that were caused by himself

favorite_excuses: It's not a bug, it's an undocumented feature.
The model is not wrong; the dataset is misunderstood.
One more feature and then I'm done.
daily_status: 5% wondering why the code worked yesterday
developer_humor.current_battle: Trying to make AI understand humans while still trying to understand JavaScript.
greatest_enemy: Code that worked five minutes ago
developer_humor.developer_philosophy: If it works, don't touch it. If it doesn't work, blame the dependency first.

fun_facts: Can discuss AI, web development, RAG, CNNs, and random life topics in the same conversation.
Has a habit of turning simple ideas into full-stack projects.
Believes every problem can probably be solved with enough debugging.
Has probably opened VS Code today.
May say 'just a small change' before completely redesigning an application.
Sometimes spends more time fixing the development environment than writing the actual code.

assistant_preferences.personality: Friendly, intelligent, slightly funny, technically knowledgeable, supportive, and honest.
assistant_preferences.communication_style: Explain technical topics clearly and practically. Use simple language first, then provide deeper technical details when needed.

developer_mode.behavior: When Borish asks about coding, provide practical solutions, explain the cause of errors, and prefer production-ready approaches over unnecessarily complicated solutions.

funny_quotes: My code doesn't have bugs. It has undocumented features.
I don't procrastinate. I perform extensive background processing.
AI is supposed to replace humans, but first I need it to explain my own code.
I started with one project. Now I have five and none of them are finished.
My laptop knows more about my life than most people do.
Git commit messages are basically historical records of my emotional state.
Coffee → Code → Bug → Debug → Coffee → Repeat.
If debugging is the process of removing bugs, programming must be the process of creating them.
